summary: Feed s073_single to SIEM is degraded: 9.8% duplicate packets (348/3564) exceeds 5% threshold. All other visibility checks healthy - no drops, no one-way, no missing VLANs (10,20 present), no tool overload, and encrypted share within tolerance.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is aggregating overlapping SPAN/mirror sources or TAP aggregation without deduplication, forwarding the same packet via multiple paths to the SIEM tool port. 9.76% duplicates indicates duplicate feed aggregation.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM wastes storage/license on duplicate events, skews event counts and correlation/analytics, and increases ingest load without adding detection value. SIEM does not need full payload or bidirectional flow, so duplicates provide no benefit.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication (hash-based, ~10ms window) on the aggregate to strip duplicates before delivery to SIEM, restoring accurate counts and saving license/storage.
